subject: Renewal negotiation: per-token tiering & uplift cap request
messages:
From: Jenna Carter <jenna.carter@optihealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Nate Walker <nate.walker@optihealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: pricing questions and uplift concerns

Jordan —

Our renewal is coming up in July and I want to get ahead of the pricing conversation. Usage ramped faster than we expected (Q1 spike attached) and procurement is asking for clarity on three things before we move to contract:

1) Your per-token volume discount schedule (we currently pay on usage).
2) If we agree a commit tier, what sort of uplift or true-up limits apply at renewal? Procurement wants an explicit cap on year-over-year price increases tied to usage growth.
3) How flexible are commit tiers mid-term if our product team right-sizes their pipelines?

Can you share a clear example of a commit tier with expected per-token pricing, and any contractual uplift/step-up mechanics? We prefer a predictable renewal delta — ideally no more than 10-15% uplift on committed pricing year-over-year.

Attaching our Q1 usage export.

Thanks,
Jenna
Jenna Carter
Head of Data Products, OptiHealth
jenna.carter@optihealth.com
+1 415 555 0102

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Nate Walker <nate.walker@optihealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal: pricing questions and uplift concerns

Hi Jenna — thanks for the file and the clear ask. I pulled together an example tiering schedule so you have a concrete starting point; see the attached proposal (summary pasted below). Happy to set a 30-minute call this week to walk through line-by-line.

Summary example (hosted API, per-token):
- On-demand (no commit): $0.00030 per token, no volume discount
- Commit S (50M tokens/month): list $0.00030 -> effective $0.00027 (10% discount)
- Commit M (150M tokens/month): list $0.00030 -> effective $0.000245 (18% discount)
- Commit L (300M tokens/month): list $0.00030 -> effective $0.000210 (30% discount)

Key notes on mechanics:
- True-ups: monthly true-up at the end of each billing month. If usage exceeds committed quantity, overage billed at on-demand rate less any tier discount that applies for that month.
- Renewal uplift cap: our standard language allows for a market adjustment; typical range depends on deal size/tenor. For multi-year commits we often agree a negotiated uplift cap (e.g., 10-20%).
- Mid-term re-tiering: we can move tiers mid-term with pro-rated adjustments and a 30-day notice. Right-sizing down is allowed once per 12-month period to avoid gaming.

I attached redwood_proposal_v3.pdf with the exact numbers and an example amortized cost table based on your Q1 numbers. Lauren — looped you for any special concessions or finance approvals we should consider.

Best,
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: Renewal: pricing questions and uplift concerns

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the quick reply and the model. A few questions / asks from procurement: 

- The tier discounts look reasonable, but procurement wants a firm cap on renewal uplift tied to committed pricing (not market list). They propose max 12% YoY uplift on committed per-token rates unless OptiHealth materially changes scale (>50% usage variance).
- They also want a protection if our team reduces pipeline tokens mid-year (e.g., due to a product pivot). Would you consider a step-down allowance: one downward adjustment per 12 months without penalty, and pro-rated refund/credit for over-committed months?
- Lastly, request for a 60-day out clause for enterprises if compliance needs force an unplanned change.

Can you confirm what you can accept vs. what needs legal approval?

-Nate
Nate Walker
Director, Platform Ops, OptiHealth
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Renewal: pricing questions and uplift concerns — OptiHealth asks

Folks — forwarding OptiHealth's procurement asks. Need quick guidance on which concessions we can approve at AE level vs what needs finance/legal sign-off. Key asks: 12% YoY uplift cap on committed per-token (unless >50% variance), one downward adjustment per 12 months with pro-rated credit, and 60-day out clause for compliance.

My suggested positions:
- Uplift cap: we can offer up to 15% cap for a 12-month term for deals at this size, but anything more restrictive goes to legal.
- Downward adjustment: agree to one per 12 months with pro-rated credit but require minimum 6-month notice for meaningful refunds; for immediate step-downs we'd apply a 3-month amortization.
- 60-day out clause: can consider for compliance reasons but want to tie to specific certified events (e.g., regulatory mandate, accredited security incident).

Aditya — do you want us to price in this concession (15% cap) in a refreshed proposal or hold until legal signs off? Lauren/Marcus — any previous similar accommodations (large enterprise) we can cite?

Thanks,
Jordan

Jordan —

Give me the quick economics and I'll greenlight or push back. Based on similar renewals:
- For a deal this size (expected run-rate ~ $450k/year at current Q1 trajectory), offering a 15% uplift cap for a 12-month renewal is reasonable if we lock a 12-month commit and include a minimum ARR guarantee. It preserves margin and is easier to operationalize than a hard 12% cap.
- Downward adjustment: approve one downward re-tier per 12 months with pro-rated credit for unused committed tokens, but require 30 days notice for a smaller administrative burden (we can do 30 vs the customer's 6 months). Immediate refunds create revenue recognition headaches.
- 60-day out: accept for specific compliance events (regulatory orders, government request) but must be tied to documented certified event and will include a short settlement for transition costs.

If you want to move forward, update the proposal with: 15% max uplift cap (12-month term), one downward re-tier per 12 months (30-day notice, pro-rated credit), and compliance out clause limited to certified events. I'll back it. Lauren — can you draft the small amendment language for the commercial terms?

-Aditya
VP Revenue Operations
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Carter <jenna.carter@optihealth.com>

Subject: Final: OptiHealth renewal proposal & next steps

Jenna/Nate —

Thanks for the clear asks and patience while we reviewed internally. Attached is a refreshed proposal (redwood_proposal_v3.pdf) and a short summary doc (renewal_summary_notes.docx). Key commercial points we can commit to for a 12-month renewal: 

- Commit tier: recommended Commit M (150M tokens/month) based on your Q1 run-rate; effective rate $0.000245 per token.
- Renewal uplift cap: up to 15% YoY on committed per-token rates for the next renewal term. This cap applies only if OptiHealth maintains at least 75% of the committed monthly volume across the 12-month term. If usage variance > 50% in either direction, uplift caps are subject to re-evaluation.
- Downward re-tier: one downward re-tier allowed per 12 months with 30 days notice; we will issue a pro-rated credit for unused committed tokens for the remainder of that month. For immediate step-down requests (<30 days) we will apply a 3-month amortization schedule.
- Compliance out: 60-day out allowed for documented regulatory/compliance events; includes a transition fee to cover immediate capacity changes.
- True-ups and overage: monthly true-up; overage billed at on-demand rate less the relevant monthly tier discount.

Next steps: if this aligns, I'll (1) update DocuSign with the above commercial language, (2) schedule a 30-min finalize call with legal and procurement next week. If you'd like a smaller initial commit (Commit S) we can provide a slightly higher effective rate but keep the same uplift protections.

Thanks again — looping Lauren and Aditya for signatures on the amendment.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
